name: Everest Three Passes Trek
alt_names: Kongma La, Cho La and Renjo La Trek
sub_region: Solukhumbu District, Koshi Province (Sagarmatha National Park, Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality)

difficulty.notes: Three passes above 5,300 m plus EBC, Kala Patthar and Gokyo Ri. Kongma La is the highest and longest day (7-10 h, no lodges or water between Chhukung and Lobuche); Cho La crosses a small glacier with a steep descent, where microspikes/light crampons are commonly advised; Renjo La is generally the easiest. Previous high-altitude trekking experience recommended.

duration_days.basis: Full trip Kathmandu-Kathmandu (about 17 trekking days Lukla-Lukla)
duration_days.notes: Classic direction is anticlockwise (Kongma La first) for gradual acclimatisation. Shortened versions skip Kongma La (two passes) or combine Thame-Lukla in one long day. Clockwise (Renjo La first) is possible but acclimatises less gradually.

max_altitude_point: Kala Patthar (highest pass: Kongma La 5,535 m)
start_point: Kathmandu (fly to Lukla, or via Manthali/Ramechhap in peak seasons)

itinerary.route: Acclimatisation day: Hotel Everest View / Khumjung

itinerary.notes: Optional afternoon hike toward Chhukung Ri.

itinerary.route: Chhukung - Kongma La (5,535 m) - Khumbu Glacier - Lobuche
Lobuche - Gorak Shep - Everest Base Camp - Gorak Shep

itinerary.notes: Pass 2; glacier section near the top; very early start.
Pass 3; some itineraries continue to Marlung (about 4,210 m).
Thame: Tenzing Norgay's home village and monastery.

best_seasons.notes: Passes can be snowbound in winter and early spring; Cho La conditions (ice, snow) vary most. Monsoon brings cloud and slippery moraine.

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person per entry (SAARC NPR 1,500; under 10 free)

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Trek-Card
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person (SAARC and Chinese nationals NPR 2,000)

guide_requirements: Conflicting. NTB lists the Three Passes trek among routes requiring a licensed guide and TIMS card since 31 March 2023, but Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality rejected the rule in April 2023 and uses its own Trek-Card; 2026 enforcement UNVERIFIED. Route-finding on the passes (especially Kongma La and Cho La) makes a guide strongly advisable regardless.

flights: Peak-season diversion via Manthali (Ramechhap): roughly spring Chaitra-Jestha and autumn first week of Ashwin to 15 Mangsir; Manthali-Lukla about 20 min
drives: Kathmandu - Manthali about 4-5 h when Lukla flights are diverted
logistics.notes: Very basic lodges at Dzongla, Thagnak (Dragnag) and Lungden. No lodge between Chhukung and Lobuche on the Kongma La day.

highlights: Three high passes: Kongma La, Cho La, Renjo La
Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar
Quiet Bhote Koshi valley and Thame village on the return
risks: High altitude for an extended period (multiple nights above 4,700 m)
Cho La glacier: ice, rockfall and a steep descent
Long remote pass days with limited rescue access
Weather closing passes (snow) and Lukla flight disruption

acclimatization.notes: Chhukung short day also helps before Kongma La.

unverified: Kala Patthar height: 5,545 m commonly listed; GPS readings of about 5,644 m reported (Wikipedia).
Pass heights are from operator sources only (Kongma La 5,535 m, Cho La 5,420 m, Renjo La 5,360 m); one source gives Kongma La as 5,530 m. Not checked against an official survey.
Current (2026) enforcement of the national licensed-guide rule in Khumbu.
